items.title: Curves, regular causal curves and future timelike worldlines in affine Minkowski space
items.statement: Let (A,V,eta,C^+) be an oriented time-oriented affine Minkowski space (def-sr-affine-minkowski-model) and let I be an order-convex subset of R with at least two elements (def-interval); a curve of the model is a map x: I -> A. (a) Derivative and regularity of the parametrization. For s in I and h nonzero with s + h in I the difference quotient (x(s+h) - x(s))/h is an element of V, the displacement from x(s) to x(s+h) divided by the real number h; the curve is differentiable at s when the limit of these quotients as h -> 0 exists in the finite-dimensional real vector space V, and then this limit, written x'(s) in V, is the tangent vector of x at s. If x_A: A -> R^4 is the chart of an inertial frame (def-inertial-frame-and-inertial-chart), then x is differentiable at s exactly when the R^4-valued map x_A o x is differentiable at s in the sense of def-vector-valued-derivative-and-integral, and then x'(s) = E((x_A o x)'(s)), where E: R^4 -> V is the frame isomorphism; this does not depend on the inertial chart used, because inertial chart transitions are affine, hence smooth (lem-affine-minkowski-charts-form-a-smooth-atlas), and all norms on the finite-dimensional V give the same limit. The curve is C^1 when it is differentiable at every point of I and the derivative map s |-> x'(s), I -> V, is continuous (def-vector-valued-functions-limits-and-continuity); it is C^k for k >= 1 when x' is C^{k-1}. A curve on a compact interval [a,b] contained in I is piecewise C^1 when there is a finite partition a = s_0 < s_1 < ... < s_m = b such that x is C^1 on every open subinterval (s_{i-1},s_i) and the finite one-sided difference-quotient derivatives at both ends of every piece exist in V. These are limits of (x(t+h)-x(t))/h over the relevant side of the piece, not assertions that x'(s) has a limit as s approaches a corner. Their finiteness implies continuity of x at the corners. No continuous extension of the open-piece derivative is required. Derivatives at the endpoints of I are the one-sided difference-quotient limits over I. (b) Causal character. Let x be differentiable at s in I. Then x is regular at s if x'(s) is not the zero vector; x is timelike (respectively null, spacelike, causal) at s if the vector x'(s) is timelike (respectively null, spacelike, causal) in the sense of def-causal-classification-of-lorentz-vectors, and x is future-directed at s if x'(s) is future timelike or future null in the sense of def-time-orientation-and-future-causal-sets. The zero vector has no causal character, so only a regular curve has a causal character at s. (c) Worldlines. A future timelike worldline (massive worldline) is a C^1 curve x: I -> A with x'(s) future timelike for every s in I; a future causal curve (respectively a future null curve) is a C^1 curve with x'(s) future causal (respectively future null) for every s in I. A piecewise C^1 worldline is a piecewise C^1 curve whose tangents at every point of each open smooth piece and whose finite one-sided difference-quotient tangents at both endpoints of every piece are future timelike, and a C^k worldline is a worldline whose parametrization is C^k; C^2 regularity is what makes the four-acceleration of this page available. The parametrization is part of the curve: the image of a future timelike worldline is also the image of the past-directed curve s |-> x(-s), which is not a worldline of this model, and no worldline or clock claim is attached to it. The definition asserts the existence of no worldline beyond those given by an explicit formula.
items.strategy: A definition item: it fixes the curve, regularity and causal-character language on which the page's items rest, and makes no proof claim beyond well-definedness. Obligations: (i) the difference quotient is an element of V because the affine action gives a displacement for every ordered pair of events, and the limit is taken in the finite-dimensional real vector space V, so no norm has to be chosen; (ii) the identification with the coordinate calculus and the independence of x'(s) and of C^k from the inertial chart are justified by the affine, hence smooth, chart transitions of lem-affine-minkowski-charts-form-a-smooth-atlas, with the published vector-valued derivative of def-vector-valued-derivative-and-integral as the coordinate calculus; (iii) continuity of x' is continuity of a V-valued map (def-vector-valued-functions-limits-and-continuity), and one-sided derivatives at endpoints are limits over the domain I as in def-vector-valued-derivative-and-integral; (iv) causal character and the future/past alternative are those of the model's vector classification and time orientation, with the zero vector excluded, so regularity is implicit in every causal character; (v) null and spacelike curves are distinguished from massive worldlines and are used later only to delimit the proper-time construction. No choice principle is used: all objects are finite-dimensional or explicitly parametrized. In the piecewise clause, a finite one-sided quotient derivative v gives x(t+h)-x(t)=h(v+o(1)), proving one-sided endpoint continuity directly. It does not imply convergence of the interior derivative; no such hypothesis is added. The timelike condition applies at every smooth point and to each side of a corner, and excludes zero tangents.

items.title: Improper integrability and endpoint increments of weak piecewise future causal curves
items.statement:
Let $x : [a,b] \to A$, $a < b$, be a piecewise $C^{1}$ curve in the sense of
[[def-sr-regular-causal-curve-and-worldline]], with a finite partition
$a = s_0 < \cdots < s_m = b$, $C^{1}$ on each open piece and finite one-sided
difference-quotient derivatives at both ends of each piece. Assume its tangents
are nonzero future causal at every open-piece point and at each one-sided
endpoint.

In any inertial chart ([[def-inertial-frame-and-inertial-chart]]) write
$y = (y^{0},z)$, $z \in \mathbb{R}^{3}$, for the coordinate path. On a piece
$(\alpha,\beta)$, choose $r \in (\alpha,\beta)$; for a function $g$ continuous
there, write

$$\int_{(\alpha,\beta)} g \;:=\; \lim_{u \downarrow \alpha} \int_u^{r} g \;+\; \lim_{v \uparrow \beta} \int_r^{v} g$$

when both limits are finite. Then:

**(a)** $y$ is continuous on $[\alpha,\beta]$, $y^{0'} \ge |z'| \ge 0$ on
$(\alpha,\beta)$, and $y^{0'} > 0$ there.

**(b)** Every coordinate derivative is absolutely improperly Riemann integrable
(its absolute value has finite improper integral), and its signed improper
integral equals the corresponding endpoint increment. The continuous functions
$|z'|$ and $f = \sqrt{(y^{0'})^{2} - |z'|^{2}} = \sqrt{-\eta(x',x')}$ have
finite nonnegative improper integrals, with
$\int_{(\alpha,\beta)} f \le \int_{(\alpha,\beta)} y^{0'} = y^{0}(\beta) - y^{0}(\alpha)$.

**(c)** The improper values are independent of $r$, additive under subdivision,
and the finite piece sums are independent of the admissible partition.

**(d)** $D = x(b)-x(a)$ is nonzero future causal: $D^{0} > 0$ and
$|D_{\mathrm{spatial}}| \le D^{0}$ in every inertial chart. If some interior or
one-sided endpoint tangent is future timelike, then $D$ is future timelike.
Coordinate time is strictly increasing on every nondegenerate subinterval. The
integrals need not be ordinary closed-piece Riemann integrals. No
derivative-limit hypothesis, Lebesgue-integration premise, clock identification,
or choice principle is used.
items.strategy: Complete local adaptation of the flat future-cone integral argument, with endpoint integrability supplied rather than assumed. (a) Finite quotient derivative v at an endpoint gives x(t+h)-x(t)=h(v+o(1)), hence endpoint continuity; C1 gives interior continuity. The future cone coordinate criterion gives y0'>=|z'| and y0'>0 on each open piece. The square root is continuous on nonnegative reals: positive arguments use thm-real-power-continuity-and-derivatives with exponent 1/2; at zero, 0<=t<epsilon^2 implies 0<=sqrt(t)<epsilon. Thus the spatial norm and causal density are continuous even at a null tangent or a zero spatial component. Since y0'>=|z'|>=0, their squared values lie between 0 and (y0')^2, giving 0<=f<=y0' by the nonnegative square-root order. (b) On every alpha<u<v<beta, the derivative is continuous on [u,v], so thm-continuous-implies-integrable and thm-ftc-second-part give integral_u^v yj'=yj(v)-yj(u). Fix r inside. For y0' the left and right limits are y0(r)-y0(alpha) and y0(beta)-y0(r), finite by endpoint continuity and nonnegative. For any continuous 0<=g<=y0', the left truncation integrals are increasing as u decreases, bounded above by y0(r)-y0(alpha); completeness supplies their supremum S. Given epsilon>0 choose u* with integral_u*^r g>S-epsilon; every alpha<u<u* then has integral_u^r g between S-epsilon and S, proving the limit S. The right side is identical. Apply this to |yj'|, |z'| and f; all are continuous inside and bounded above by y0'. Signed coordinate integrals converge by the truncated FTC and endpoint continuity; thus each derivative is absolutely improperly integrable and has the exact endpoint increment. (c) Ordinary integral additivity on truncations and finite limits show independence of r and additivity under each interior cut. Any two admissible finite partitions have a common refinement, so all finite sums agree. (d) On truncations, the vector-integral norm inequality gives |z(v)-z(u)|<=integral_u^v |z'|<=integral_u^v y0'. Pass to endpoints and sum with the Euclidean triangle inequality to obtain |D_spatial|<=D0. Positive y0' on a compact interior interval gives a positive time increment, and nonnegativity on the rest gives D0>0; apply the same argument to any nondegenerate restriction for strict time monotonicity. At an interior timelike tangent, y0'-|z'| is continuous and positive in a compact interior neighborhood, so its integral is positive and the inequality becomes strict. At a left endpoint with timelike one-sided quotient v, (y(alpha+h)-y(alpha))/h tends to v, so for some h>0 that quotient is future timelike by openness of the cone. This subdisplacement is future timelike, and the remaining subdisplacement is future causal by the already proved non-strict inequality; adding their coordinates yields a future timelike sum. At a right endpoint use (y(beta)-y(beta-h))/h similarly. At a corner use the corresponding adjacent piece. This proves the endpoint-only timelike clause without continuity of the derivative at the corner. No closed-piece derivative integrability or countable choice is assumed.

items.title: Proper time along a future timelike worldline
items.statement:
Let $c > 0$ be a fixed real number, the conversion constant of the model, and
let $x : I \to A$ be a $C^{1}$ future timelike worldline
([[def-sr-regular-causal-curve-and-worldline]]).

**The integrand.** The function

$$g_x : I \to \mathbb{R}, \qquad g_x(s) := -\eta\bigl(x'(s),x'(s)\bigr),$$

is continuous and strictly positive. For continuity, fix an inertial frame and
write $y := x_A \circ x$ for the coordinate path; by the derivative and regularity definition in
[[def-sr-regular-causal-curve-and-worldline]] the $\mathbb{R}^{4}$-valued map
$y'$ is continuous, so each component $y'^{a}$, $a \in \{0,1,2,3\}$, is a
continuous real function ([[thm-componentwise-limits-and-continuity]]). In the
$\eta$-orthonormal basis underlying the frame one has
$\eta(e_a,e_b) = \operatorname{diag}(-1,1,1,1)_{ab}$
([[def-inertial-frame-and-inertial-chart]]), whence

$$g_x(s) = -\eta\bigl(x'(s),x'(s)\bigr) = \bigl(y'^{0}(s)\bigr)^{2} - \bigl(y'^{1}(s)\bigr)^{2} - \bigl(y'^{2}(s)\bigr)^{2} - \bigl(y'^{3}(s)\bigr)^{2},$$

a finite sum of products of continuous real functions, hence continuous
([[thm-algebra-of-continuous-functions]], [[def-continuity-real]],
[[lem-lorentz-form-has-orthonormal-basis]]). Strict positivity
$g_x(s) = -\eta(x'(s),x'(s)) > 0$ is exactly the future timelike hypothesis on
$x'(s)$ ([[def-causal-classification-of-lorentz-vectors]]).

**The proper-time function.** Hence $u \mapsto \sqrt{g_x(u)}$ is continuous on
$I$: the square root is the power $t^{1/2}$ of [[def-rational-power]], which is
continuous and differentiable on $(0,\infty)$
([[thm-real-power-continuity-and-derivatives]]), and it is composed with the
continuous positive function $g_x$
([[thm-composition-of-continuous-functions]]); consequently it is Riemann
integrable on every compact subinterval of $I$
([[thm-continuous-implies-integrable]], [[def-interval]]). For $s_0, s \in I$
the **proper time from $s_0$ to $s$** is

$$\tau(s) := c^{-1} \int_{s_0}^{s} \sqrt{-\eta\bigl(x'(u),x'(u)\bigr)}\; du,$$

the integral being taken with oriented limits as in [[def-oriented-integral]];
for $a < b$ in $I$ this reads

$$\tau(b) - \tau(a) = c^{-1} \int_a^b \sqrt{-\eta\bigl(x'(u),x'(u)\bigr)}\; du,$$

by oriented additivity ([[thm-additivity-over-subintervals]]); equivalently,
the increment is the integral function with base point $a$ of the density
$c^{-1}\sqrt{g_x}$, evaluated at $b$ on $[a,b]$
([[def-the-integral-function]]). Changing the base point $s_0$ changes $\tau$
by an additive constant, so the elapsed times between parameter values are
intrinsic. $\tau$ depends on the parametrized history $x$ and on the parameter
values; its invariance under increasing $C^{1}$ reparametrizations with everywhere
positive derivative is proved in
[[lem-sr-proper-time-reparametrization-invariance]].

**Straight segments.** For the straight future timelike segment
$x(s) = p + (s-s_0)(q-p)$ of [[def-sr-affine-minkowski-model]] the difference
quotients are identically the future timelike displacement $q-p$, so
$x'(s) = q-p$ and

$$\tau(b) - \tau(a) = c^{-1} \sqrt{-\eta(q-p,q-p)}\,(b-a),$$

the straight-segment proper time of the model's coordinate conventions.

**Scope.** The construction is restricted to future timelike worldlines: on a
future null curve the length density vanishes identically, so its integral
is constant; a zero density at one isolated point does not imply constancy; for a spacelike
curve $-\eta(x',x')$ is negative and the square root is not a real number; and
for a past-directed timelike curve the same integral is defined but is not
attached to a worldline of this model. The construction asserts nothing about
physical clock readings.
items.strategy: Definition item with well-definedness obligations: (i) the integrand is the composition of the continuous map s |-> x'(s), the continuous quadratic form v |-> -eta(v,v) (checked in coordinates in an eta-orthonormal basis, since eta is bilinear on the finite-dimensional V) and the continuous power t |-> t^{1/2} on (0,inf); (ii) strict positivity of g_x is exactly the future timelike hypothesis, so the square root is a positive real number on all of I; (iii) existence of the integral on compact subintervals is thm-continuous-implies-integrable, and the oriented convention makes tau(s_0) = 0 and reverses the sign when the endpoints are exchanged; (iv) the base point enters only additively, so elapsed times between parameter values are intrinsic; (v) the straight-segment consistency is a direct evaluation: x' is constant on a straight segment and the integrand is c^{-1} sqrt(-eta(q-p,q-p)) times the parameter length. No choice principle is used. The item deliberately does not assert that tau is differentiable or invertible (that is lem-sr-proper-time-parametrization) nor that a physical clock reads tau (that belongs to the adopted physical interpretation).

items.title: Total proper time of a piecewise C^1 future timelike worldline
items.statement: Let c>0 be the conversion constant of def-sr-proper-time and let x:[a,b]->A, a<b, be a piecewise C^1 future timelike worldline in the weak sense of def-sr-regular-causal-curve-and-worldline: x is C^1 on each open piece of a finite partition a=s_0<...<s_m=b, its interior tangents and finite one-sided difference-quotient endpoint tangents are future timelike, and continuous extension of the derivative is not assumed. (i) On each open piece let g_i(t)=sqrt(-eta(x'(t),x'(t)))>0. Define its two-ended improper Riemann integral by the convention of lem-sr-weak-piecewise-causal-integrability. That lemma proves each value finite and nonnegative; it is positive since g_i is positive and continuous on a compact interior subinterval. (ii) Define total proper time by Delta tau_[a,b](x)=c^{-1} sum_i integral_(s_(i-1),s_i) g_i. The finite sum is independent of the partition, by subdivision additivity and a common refinement. It is independent of the inertial chart because eta and the tangent are chart independent; constant Lorentz changes preserve the density already on each proper truncation. (iii) Define the based proper-time function tau_x(s)=Delta tau_[s0,s](x) for s>=s0, and tau_x(s)=-Delta tau_[s,s0](x) for s<s0, with tau_x(s0)=0, using restrictions and oriented limits. It is strictly increasing, and changing s0 changes only an additive constant. (iv) Corner hypothesis (H) is the special case in which each open-piece derivative has finite limits at both ends and thus extends continuously to the closed piece. Those limits equal the one-sided quotient derivatives. Under (H), each g_i extends continuously and positively to the closed piece, its improper integral equals its ordinary Riemann integral there, and the same finite-sum formula applies. In particular if x is globally C^1 on [a,b], Delta tau(x)=tau(b)-tau(a) of def-sr-proper-time. (v) Delta tau(x)>0. If on piece i the tangent is a constant future timelike vector d_i, the contribution is c^{-1}(s_i-s_(i-1))sqrt(-eta(d_i,d_i)); this gives the finite sum of straight-segment proper times. (vi) Additivity over concatenation: for a<b<d, restrictions of a weak piecewise worldline x on [a,d] satisfy Delta tau_[a,d](x)=Delta tau_[a,b](x)+Delta tau_[b,d](x). Insert b in the partition and use (ii). The definition supplies metric time only; identification with an ideal clock reading is the separate physical clock postulate. No global C^1 inverse, tangent at a kink, or four-acceleration at a kink is asserted.
items.strategy: Well-definedness is lem-sr-weak-piecewise-causal-integrability: endpoint continuity, finite improper integrals dominated in an inertial chart by the nonnegative time derivative, truncated FTC and partition independence. Strict positivity follows by a compact interior neighborhood on which g_i is positive and continuous. Refinements split each integral, and a common refinement gives independence of the finite partition. Restriction/additivity also give the based function, strict increase and base-point constants. Under (H), if the extended derivative is f_i, truncated FTC gives x(v)-x(u)=integral_u^v f_i. Passing u to the endpoint shows that the one-sided difference quotient is the average of f_i over a shrinking interval and therefore tends to its continuous endpoint value; thus the extension equals the finite quotient tangent. The extended density is continuous and strictly positive on the compact closed piece. Its bounded omitted endpoint tails tend to zero, so its improper value equals the ordinary Riemann value. Global C1 is the one-piece (H) case and agrees with def-sr-proper-time. Constant tangents give the displayed straight-segment calculation directly. All steps are finite-dimensional one-variable real analysis and use no choice principle; no physical premise supplies mathematical integrability.

items.title: Proper time is invariant under regular increasing weak piecewise changes of parameter
items.statement: Let c>0 and let x:[a,b]->A be a weak piecewise C^1 future timelike worldline. Let phi:[u,v]->[a,b] be an increasing continuous surjection, C^1 on the open pieces of a finite partition, with phi'>0 at every interior smooth point and finite positive one-sided difference-quotient derivatives at both endpoints of each piece. Then phi is strictly increasing with continuous inverse, y=x composed with phi is a weak piecewise C^1 future timelike worldline, and Delta tau_[u,v](y)=Delta tau_[a,b](x). The same equality holds for every pair of corresponding restricted parameter intervals; based proper-time functions differ only by their base-point constant. The relevant partition is the common refinement of phi's partition and the inverse images of x's partition points. This statement gives worldline/clock consequences only for positive derivatives, including all one-sided endpoint derivatives. It leaves intact the separate global-C^1 curve-integral identities allowing zero tangents in lem-sr-proper-time-reparametrization-invariance; a zero-tangent composition is not asserted to be a worldline.
items.strategy: On each closed piece phi is continuous and differentiable inside with phi'>0, so the mean value theorem proves strict increase there; finite concatenation gives global strict increase, and the continuous monotone bijection has continuous inverse. The finite inverse-image refinement separates all x and phi corners. Inside each refined piece componentwise chain rule gives y'=phi' x'(phi), so y' is continuous and future timelike and sqrt(-eta(y',y'))=phi' f(phi), where f=sqrt(-eta(x',x')). At each one-sided endpoint the quotient of y is the product of the corresponding quotient of x and that of phi; strict monotonicity chooses the correct side and both finite limits exist, the latter positive. Thus y has finite future timelike one-sided tangents and lies in the same weak class. On any compact interior truncation [r,s] of a refined piece, f is continuous on the compact image interval and phi' is continuous and integrable on [r,s]; thm-substitution gives integral_r^s phi' f(phi)=integral_phi(r)^phi(s) f. As r and s approach the refined endpoints, continuity and strict monotonicity of phi make the image endpoints approach the corresponding x endpoints. Both improper limits exist by lem-sr-weak-piecewise-causal-integrability for x and y, so the identity passes to the limits. Finite summation and partition independence give the full and restricted interval identities. Oriented additivity gives the based-function constant. No boundedness of the derivative near a corner is assumed and no zero tangent is admitted as a worldline.

items.title: The proper-time function is a strictly increasing C^1 parametrization with C^1 inverse
items.statement:
Let $c > 0$ and let $x : I \to A$ be a $C^{1}$ future timelike worldline
([[def-sr-regular-causal-curve-and-worldline]]) with proper-time function
$\tau(s) = c^{-1}\int_{s_0}^{s}\sqrt{-\eta(x'(u),x'(u))}\,du$ for a base point
$s_0 \in I$ ([[def-sr-proper-time]]). Then:

**(i)** $\tau$ is differentiable at every $s \in I$, with one-sided derivatives
at the endpoints of $I$, and

$$\tau'(s) = c^{-1}\sqrt{-\eta\bigl(x'(s),x'(s)\bigr)} > 0$$

for every $s \in I$; since $\tau'$ is this composition of continuous maps,
$\tau$ is $C^{1}$ on $I$.

**(ii)** $\tau$ is strictly increasing on $I$, hence injective, and its image
$J := \tau[I]$ is an order-convex subset of $\mathbb{R}$ with at least two
elements, so $\tau : I \to J$ is a bijection.

**(iii)** The inverse $\rho : J \to I$ of $\tau$ is continuous and strictly
increasing, and it is differentiable at every point $\tau(s)$ of $J$ with

$$\rho'\bigl(\tau(s)\bigr) = \frac{1}{\tau'(s)} = \frac{c}{\sqrt{-\eta(x'(s),x'(s))}} > 0 ;$$

hence $\rho$ is $C^{1}$ on $J$.

**(iv)** The reparametrized curve $y := x \circ \rho : J \to A$ is a $C^{1}$
future timelike worldline whose tangent at the proper-time parameter $\tau(s)$ is

$$(x \circ \rho)'\bigl(\tau(s)\bigr) = \frac{x'(s)}{\tau'(s)} = \frac{c\,x'(s)}{\sqrt{-\eta(x'(s),x'(s))}} ;$$

in particular $y$ is parametrized by its own proper time up to the additive
constant of the base point.
items.strategy: (i) thm-ftc-first-part applied to the continuous integrand u |-> c^{-1} sqrt(-eta(x'(u),x'(u))) on a compact neighbourhood of s (contained in I using def-interval) gives tau'(s) equal to that value, with the one-sided reading at endpoints; positivity is the future timelike hypothesis. (ii) For a < b in I, monotonicity of the integral (thm-monotonicity-of-the-integral) gives tau(b) - tau(a) >= 0, and equality would force the continuous nonnegative integrand to vanish on [a,b] (thm-nonnegative-continuous-with-zero-integral-vanishes), contradicting its strict positivity; so tau is strictly increasing and injective, and its image is order-convex and nondegenerate by cor-continuous-image-of-an-interval-is-an-interval (tau is continuous). (iii) A continuous injective map on an interval has a continuous strictly monotone inverse (thm-continuous-inverse), and the reciprocal derivative formula is thm-derivative-of-an-inverse, applicable since tau'(s) > 0; tau' continuous gives rho C^1. (iv) Differentiating componentwise in an inertial chart and applying the one-variable chain rule to each coordinate (def-vector-valued-derivative-and-integral, thm-chain-rule) gives (x o rho)' = (x' o rho) rho' at interior points, with one-sided readings at endpoints; rho' > 0 preserves future timelikeness. The base point shifts rho's argument and leaves derivatives unchanged. No choice principle is used.

items.title: Length-integral invariance under monotone C^1 maps and proper-time invariance under regular increasing maps
items.statement:
Let $c > 0$, let $x : I \to A$ be a $C^{1}$ future timelike worldline
([[def-sr-regular-causal-curve-and-worldline]]), let $a < b$ with
$[a,b] \subseteq I$, and let $c_0 < d_0$. Let
$\varphi : [c_0,d_0] \to [a,b]$ be a strictly increasing $C^{1}$ surjection,
with one-sided endpoint derivatives as in
[[def-sr-regular-causal-curve-and-worldline]].

Then $\varphi(c_0) = a$, $\varphi(d_0) = b$ and $\varphi' \ge 0$. Put
$y = x \circ \varphi$ and $f(s) = \sqrt{-\eta(x'(s),x'(s))}$. The $C^{1}$ curve
$y$ has tangent

$$y'(u) = \varphi'(u)\,x'\bigl(\varphi(u)\bigr),$$

which is future timelike exactly where $\varphi'(u) > 0$ and is the zero vector
where $\varphi'(u) = 0$. Its nonnegative length integrand

$$\sqrt{-\eta\bigl(y'(u),y'(u)\bigr)} = \varphi'(u)\,f\bigl(\varphi(u)\bigr)$$

is defined even when $y$ is not a worldline, and the broad substitution identity

$$\int_{c_0}^{d_0}\sqrt{-\eta\bigl(y'(u),y'(u)\bigr)}\;du \;=\; \int_a^b f(s)\;ds \;=\; c\bigl(\tau_x(b)-\tau_x(a)\bigr)$$

holds. If $\varphi'(u) > 0$ at every point, including the one-sided endpoint
derivatives, then $y$ is a $C^{1}$ future timelike worldline, its proper-time
function $\tau_y$ of [[def-sr-proper-time]] is defined, and
$\tau_y(d_0)-\tau_y(c_0) = \tau_x(b)-\tau_x(a)$; more generally
$\tau_y(u)-\tau_y(v) = \tau_x(\varphi(u))-\tau_x(\varphi(v))$ for all
$v,u \in [c_0,d_0]$, so $\tau_y$ and $\tau_x \circ \varphi$ differ by a
base-point constant. No $\tau_y$ is asserted for a zero-tangent curve outside
that definition.

For a strictly decreasing $C^{1}$ surjection $\varphi$ onto $[a,b]$ one has
$\varphi(c_0) = b$, $\varphi(d_0) = a$ and $\varphi' \le 0$; the tangent of $y$
is past timelike where $\varphi' < 0$ and zero where $\varphi' = 0$, so $y$ is
not a future timelike worldline, while the nonnegative length integral still
equals $\int_a^b f$: oriented substitution gives
$\int_{c_0}^{d_0}\varphi' f(\varphi) = \int_b^a f$, and
$|\varphi'| = -\varphi'$ reverses that sign.

These are mathematical curve-integral identities; physical clock reading is a
separate premise. No inverse of $\varphi$ and no nonvanishing derivative are
needed for the broad integral identities.
items.strategy: By the componentwise chain rule, including its one-sided endpoint reading, y'=phi'(x' o phi). Bilinearity gives -eta(y',y')=(phi')^2(-eta(x' o phi,x' o phi)), so the nonnegative square root is |phi'|(f o phi). The function f is continuous on I by def-sr-proper-time, and the C^1 derivative phi' is continuous and therefore Riemann integrable on its compact interval. The published thm-substitution applies with f and phi even when phi' vanishes: for increasing phi its oriented endpoints are a,b and |phi'|=phi', proving the broad integral equality. The future cone is preserved by a positive scalar; at phi'=0 the tangent is zero, which is excluded by the worldline definition. Thus only the everywhere-positive derivative case permits applying def-sr-proper-time to y. Apply substitution on every subinterval [v,u] (with oriented reversal when u<v) to prove the proper-time difference formula and base-point constant. For decreasing phi, oriented endpoints b,a give the negative integral, while |phi'|=-phi' restores the positive integral; the tangent is past timelike where the scalar is negative and zero otherwise. No inverse of phi and no nonvanishing derivative are needed for the broad integral identities. No choice principle is used.

items.title: Four-velocity and four-acceleration of a future timelike worldline
items.statement:
Let $c > 0$ and let $x : I \to A$ be a $C^{1}$ future timelike worldline with
proper-time function $\tau$ and inverse $\rho$ of
[[def-sr-proper-time]] and [[lem-sr-proper-time-parametrization]].

**(a) Four-velocity.** The **four-velocity** of $x$ is the map $U : I \to V$
defined by

$$U(s) := \frac{x'(s)}{\tau'(s)} = \frac{c\,x'(s)}{\sqrt{-\eta(x'(s),x'(s))}} ;$$

equivalently, $U(s)$ is the tangent at parameter value $s$ of the proper-time
parametrized worldline $x \circ \rho$, read at the proper-time parameter
$\tau(s)$: by clause (iv) of [[lem-sr-proper-time-parametrization]],
$(x \circ \rho)'(\tau(s)) = x'(s)/\tau'(s) = U(s)$. The map $U$ is continuous,
$U(s)$ is future timelike for every $s \in I$, and $U$ does not depend on the
base point chosen for $\tau$ (changing the base point adds a constant to
$\tau$).

**(b) Four-acceleration.** If $x$ is $C^{2}$, that is, $x'$ is differentiable
with continuous derivative ([[def-sr-regular-causal-curve-and-worldline]]), the
**four-acceleration** of $x$ is the map $A : I \to V$ defined by

$$A(s) := \frac{U'(s)}{\tau'(s)} = \frac{c\,U'(s)}{\sqrt{-\eta(x'(s),x'(s))}} ;$$

equivalently, $A(s)$ is the derivative with respect to the proper-time parameter
of the four-velocity along the worldline: by the chain rule,
$A(s) = (U \circ \rho)'(\tau(s))$. The map $A$ is continuous.

**(c) Observer.** The **dimensionless four-velocity** of $x$ is $u := U/c$. A
**point observer** of the model at an event is a future unit timelike vector
$n \in V$, $\eta(n,n) = -1$ ([[def-causal-classification-of-lorentz-vectors]],
[[def-time-orientation-and-future-causal-sets]]); the four-velocity of the
observer's own worldline, the straight future timelike line through the event
with tangent $cn$, is $cn$ at each of its events.

**(d) Names and scope.** The names four-velocity and four-acceleration are the
model's names for $U$ and $A$; the physical interpretation, including the units
in which $U$ and $A$ are measured, is supplied with the coordinate conventions
of the framework and is not part of the affine geometry. The definition makes no
claim that $U$ has norm $-c^{2}$ or that $A$ is orthogonal to $U$; those are
proved in [[thm-sr-proper-time-and-observer-decomposition]].
items.strategy: Definition item: it introduces the two derived vector fields along a worldline and fixes their well-definedness. Obligations: (i) the division by tau'(s) is legitimate because tau' > 0 by lem-sr-proper-time-parametrization; (ii) the identification U(s) = (x o rho)'(tau(s)) is the chain rule applied componentwise in an inertial chart (def-vector-valued-derivative-and-integral, thm-chain-rule), and it shows that U is the tangent field of the proper-time parametrized worldline; (iii) continuity of U follows from continuity of x' and tau' and continuity of division by the positive function tau'; (iv) A is defined only when x is C^2, in which case U' exists; (v) neither the norm of U nor the orthogonality of A with U is asserted here, so the definition cannot be used as if those identities were definitional. No choice principle is used. Under C2, g_x is C1 by its finite quadratic expression and tau prime is C1 by square-root differentiation on g_x>0; quotient and product derivatives make U prime and A continuous.

items.title: Norms of four-velocity and four-acceleration, and the observer rest-space decomposition
items.statement:
Let $c > 0$ and let $(A,V,\eta,C^{+})$ be an oriented time-oriented affine
Minkowski space ([[def-sr-affine-minkowski-model]]).

**(a) Norm of the four-velocity.** Let $x : I \to A$ be a $C^{1}$ future
timelike worldline with four-velocity $U$
([[def-sr-four-velocity-and-four-acceleration]]). Then
$\eta(U(s),U(s)) = -c^{2}$ for every $s \in I$; equivalently the dimensionless
four-velocity $u = U/c$ satisfies $\eta(u,u) = -1$, and $U(s)$ is future
timelike. Thus the dimensionless four-velocity lies on the future unit
hyperboloid $\{v \in C^{+}:\eta(v,v)=-1\}$.

**(b) Orthogonality of the four-acceleration.** If $x$ is $C^{2}$ at $s$, then
$\eta(U(s),A(s)) = 0$: the four-acceleration has no component along the
four-velocity; if in addition $A(s) \ne 0$, then $A(s)$ is spacelike.

**(c) Rest space and projection.** Let $n \in V$ be future unit timelike,
$\eta(n,n) = -1$, and put $n^{\perp} := \{\,v \in V : \eta(n,v) = 0\,\}$
([[def-lorentz-orthogonality-and-orthogonal-complement]]). Then $n^{\perp}$ is a
3-dimensional linear subspace of $V$, the restriction of $\eta$ to $n^{\perp}$
is positive definite, and the map $h : V \to V$, $h(v) := v + \eta(n,v)\,n$, is
linear, idempotent with $h \circ h = h$, has image $n^{\perp}$ and kernel
$\operatorname{span}(n)$, satisfies $h(n) = 0$ and $\eta(n,h(v)) = 0$ for all
$v \in V$, and every $v \in V$ has the unique decomposition
$v = -\eta(n,v)\,n + h(v)$. Moreover $|w| := \sqrt{\eta(w,w)}$ defines a norm
on $n^{\perp}$.

**(d) Relative velocity and Lorentz factor.** Let $n$ and $u$ be future unit
timelike vectors, put $\gamma := -\eta(n,u)$ and $w := c\,h(u)/\gamma$. Then
$\gamma \ge 1$, $w$ lies in $n^{\perp}$,
$u = \gamma\,(n + w/c)$, $|w|^{2} = c^{2}(1-\gamma^{-2}) < c^{2}$,
$\gamma = (1-|w|^{2}/c^{2})^{-1/2}$, and $\gamma = 1$ if and only if $u = n$.
The vector $w$ is the velocity of a worldline with four-velocity $cu$ relative
to the observer $n$, and $\gamma$ is its Lorentz factor.

**(e) Coordinate form.** Let $(o;e_0,\dots,e_3)$ be an inertial frame and let
$y$ be a $C^{1}$ future timelike worldline whose inertial coordinates are
$t \mapsto (ct,r(t))$, with coordinate velocity $w(t) := r'(t)$ in
$\mathbb{R}^{3}$ and, when $y$ is $C^{2}$, coordinate acceleration
$a(t) := w'(t)$. Then $|w(t)| < c$, the four-velocity is
$U = \gamma_w\,(c,w)$ with $\gamma_w := (1-|w|^{2}/c^{2})^{-1/2}$, and the
four-acceleration is $A = \gamma_w\,\frac{d}{dt}\bigl(\gamma_w(c,w)\bigr)$, so
that

$$A^{0} = \gamma_w^{4}\,\frac{w \cdot a}{c}, \qquad A_{\mathrm{vec}} = \gamma_w^{2}\,a + \gamma_w^{4}\,\frac{(w \cdot a)\,w}{c^{2}} ;$$

consequently
$\eta(A,A) = \gamma_w^{4}|a|^{2} + \gamma_w^{6}(w \cdot a)^{2}/c^{2} \ge 0$,
with $\eta(A,A) = 0$ if and only if $a = 0$, and $\eta(U,A) = 0$. For the
observer $n = e_0$ of the chart, clauses (c) and (d) specialize to
$\gamma = \gamma_w$ and $w_{\mathrm{rel}} = (0,w)$ in the frame coordinates, identified with $w$ via the spatial basis.

**(f) Scope.** The statement is a theorem about the affine Minkowski model with
a fixed positive constant $c$; it asserts no clock reading and identifies no
physical four-velocity. No choice principle is used.
items.strategy: Proof in dependency order; the hard part is (c), which is pure algebra plus one coordinate computation, and the remaining clauses follow from it. (c) Fix an eta-orthonormal basis with e_0 future timelike (lem-lorentz-form-has-orthonormal-basis; use an inertial frame of def-inertial-frame-and-inertial-chart). Write n = n^0 e_0 + n_s and v = v^0 e_0 + v_s with n_s,v_s in S = span(e_1,e_2,e_3), where eta restricts to the positive definite delta with norm |.| (def-spatial-euclidean-structure-of-an-inertial-frame). From eta(n,n) = -(n^0)^2 + |n_s|^2 = -1 one gets (n^0)^2 = 1 + |n_s|^2 > 0. For v with eta(n,v) = -n^0 v^0 + delta(n_s,v_s) = 0 one has v^0 = delta(n_s,v_s)/n^0, hence eta(v,v) = -(v^0)^2 + |v_s|^2 = |v_s|^2 - delta(n_s,v_s)^2/(n^0)^2 >= |v_s|^2 (1 - |n_s|^2/(n^0)^2) = |v_s|^2/(n^0)^2 >= 0 by the finite Cauchy-Schwarz inequality for delta (thm-cauchy-schwarz-finite); equality forces |v_s| = 0 and then v^0 = 0, so v = 0 and the restriction is positive definite. The map v_s |-> v^0 e_0 + v_s with v^0 = delta(n_s,v_s)/n^0 is a linear bijection S -> n^perp, so n^perp is 3-dimensional. The properties of h are immediate from bilinearity of eta (def-lorentz-form-and-inertia, def-linear-map): eta(n,h(v)) = eta(n,v) + eta(n,v)eta(n,n) = 0, so h(v) lies in n^perp; h(n) = n + eta(n,n)n = 0; h(h(v)) = h(v) + eta(n,h(v))n = h(v); and v = -eta(n,v)n + h(v) is unique because the two summands lie in span(n) and n^perp, which meet only in 0. (a) By def-sr-four-velocity-and-four-acceleration, U = x'/tau' with tau' = c^{-1} sqrt(-eta(x',x')), so eta(U,U) = eta(x',x')/(tau')^2 = eta(x',x') c^2/(-eta(x',x')) = -c^2; timelikeness and the future direction of U follow from those of x' and positivity of 1/tau'. (b) eta(U,U) is the constant -c^2 along a C^2 worldline; differentiating componentwise in an eta-orthonormal basis with thm-algebra-of-derivatives gives 0 = (d/ds) eta(U,U) = 2 eta(U,U'), hence eta(U,U') = 0, and dividing by tau' > 0 gives eta(U,A) = 0. If A(s) is nonzero, then A(s) lies in (U(s)/c)^perp, a positive definite space by (c), so eta(A,A) > 0: A(s) is spacelike. (d) By (c), h(u) lies in n^perp and u = gamma n + h(u) with gamma = -eta(n,u). First, gamma > 0: in the inertial frame of (c), future timelikeness of n and u gives n^0 > |n_s| and u^0 > |u_s| (lem-timelike-cone-has-two-convex-components), so eta(n,u) = -n^0 u^0 + delta(n_s,u_s) <= -n^0 u^0 + |n_s||u_s| < 0. Second, eta(u,u) = gamma^2 eta(n,n) + eta(h(u),h(u)) = -gamma^2 + |h(u)|^2 = -1, so |h(u)|^2 = gamma^2 - 1 >= 0, giving gamma >= 1; substituting w = c h(u)/gamma gives |w|^2 = c^2 (gamma^2-1)/gamma^2 = c^2(1 - gamma^{-2}) < c^2, and solving for gamma gives gamma = (1 - |w|^2/c^2)^{-1/2} and gamma = 1 iff h(u) = 0 iff u = n. (e) In the chart the coordinate path is t |-> (c t, r(t)), so x' = (c,w) and -eta(x',x') = c^2 - |w|^2 > 0 by future timelikeness, giving |w| < c and tau' = c^{-1} sqrt(c^2-|w|^2) = (1 - |w|^2/c^2)^{1/2} = 1/gamma_w; hence U = x'/tau' = gamma_w (c,w). For C^2 paths, d gamma_w/dt = gamma_w^3 (w.a)/c^2 by thm-real-power-continuity-and-derivatives (applied to the power -1/2) with the chain rule, and collecting terms in A = gamma_w dU/dt gives the displayed components; expanding eta(A,A) in the diagonal form and using gamma_w^2(1-|w|^2/c^2) = 1 gives eta(A,A) = gamma_w^4 |a|^2 + gamma_w^6 (w.a)^2/c^2 >= 0 with equality iff |a| = 0, and eta(U,A) = 0 agrees with (b). (f) The specialization n = e_0 is the evaluation h(u) = u - u^0 e_0 = (0, w/c gamma_w) and gamma = u^0 = gamma_w, so w_rel has coordinates (0,w), identified with w via the spatial basis. No choice principle is used; all arguments are finite-dimensional or one-variable calculus. The dimensionless vector U/c, rather than U, lies on the unit hyperboloid. On the arbitrary observer complement, expand the nonnegative quadratic eta(w-tz,w-tz) at t=eta(w,z)/eta(z,z) for z nonzero; this gives Cauchy–Schwarz and the norm triangle inequality, with zero case immediate.

items.title: Adopted free trajectories of massive particles and the clock hypothesis
items.statement:
Adopt as physical assumptions of this framework, extending the ideal-clock
reading rule of [[post-sr-ideal-clocks-and-light]] to the general worldline
calculus of this page:

**(i) Free trajectories.** A massive test particle that is subject to no
interaction (a **free particle**) has as its worldline a straight future
timelike line of the affine model ([[def-sr-affine-minkowski-model]]): there are
an event $p \in A$ and a future timelike vector $v \in V$ with
$x(s) = p + (s-s_0)v$ for $s\in I$, where $I\subseteq\mathbb R$ is a nondegenerate interval and $s_0\in I$ ([[def-sr-regular-causal-curve-and-worldline]]).
Interactions, forces and collisions are not part of this assumption: a particle
that is not free may have any future timelike worldline admitted by its own
dynamical model, and no force law is adopted here. The kinematical consequences
of this shape for the four-velocity are derived, not assumed, in
[[pthm-sr-four-velocity-norm-and-orthogonality]].

**(ii) Clock hypothesis.** An ideal clock carried along a future timelike
worldline of the model, including an accelerated one and a piecewise $C^{1}$ one
with finitely many kinks, reads between any two parameter values the proper-time
difference of [[def-sr-proper-time]] for $C^{1}$ histories and of
[[def-sr-piecewise-proper-time]] for weak piecewise $C^{1}$ histories, with no
additional term depending on acceleration, jerk or any higher derivative. A
kink is an idealization of a finite short acceleration phase whose contribution
is included through the integral on the smooth pieces, and the reading does not
depend on an increasing regular change of parameter admitted by the curve
definition — its derivatives on smooth pieces and all finite one-sided endpoint
derivatives are positive, as in
[[lem-sr-proper-time-reparametrization-invariance]] and
[[lem-sr-piecewise-proper-time-reparametrization-invariance]]. Zero-tangent
compositions are not worldlines of this model.

**(iii) Scope and qualification.** The assumptions concern ideal point
particles, ideal clocks and flat classical spacetime. They are adopted, not
proved; they are not consequences of the affine geometry, and no experiment is
claimed here to establish them. They inherit the idealizations of
[[post-sr-ideal-clocks-and-light]]: real clocks have finite resolution,
calibration and apparatus limitations, and real particles are not exactly free.
The coordinate and unit conventions are those of
[[def-sr-si-units-and-coordinate-conventions]], and inertial charts are those
of [[def-inertial-frame-and-inertial-chart]].
items.strategy: A postulate, not a theorem: it fixes the physical interpretation of straight future timelike lines as the histories of free massive test particles and makes the clock-reading rule applicable to the general worldline class of this page. Obligations: (i) straight future timelike lines are declared objects of the affine model, and each is a future timelike worldline with constant tangent (def-sr-regular-causal-curve-and-worldline); (ii) the reading rule is an identification of a physical clock reading with the mathematical proper-time difference, so def-sr-proper-time and its reparametrization invariance are the mathematical suppliers carrying the content, while the identification itself is adopted; (iii) the free-trajectory clause is deliberately silent about interactions and force laws, so it cannot be used to infer conservation laws, mass-shell relations or collision kinematics, which require the separate momentum postulate of the later energy-momentum page; (iv) the clock hypothesis is the assertion that ideal clocks have no acceleration-dependent term, so it must not be presented as following from the geometry. No proof is manufactured; the item is an adopted premise with an exact scope. The weak piecewise mathematical referent is supplied by def-sr-piecewise-proper-time and its integrability lemma, and regular increasing weak-piecewise parameter independence by lem-sr-piecewise-proper-time-reparametrization-invariance. This repairs the formulation of the already adopted clock assumption; it does not derive clock behavior or extend its empirical scope.

items.title: Four-velocity norm and four-acceleration orthogonality for the model's clocks
items.statement:
Adopt the postulates of the model: [[post-sr-inertial-covariance]] and
[[post-sr-ideal-clocks-and-light]] of the spacetime-primitives page, together
with [[post-sr-free-trajectories-and-clock-hypothesis]] of this page, and let
$c$ and the SI coordinates be those of
[[def-sr-si-units-and-coordinate-conventions]]. Let $x : I \to A$ be the
history of an ideal clock of the model, a $C^{1}$ future timelike worldline
($C^{2}$ where acceleration is used), with proper time $\tau$, four-velocity
$U = dx/d\tau$ and, when $x$ is $C^{2}$, four-acceleration $A = dU/d\tau$
([[def-sr-four-velocity-and-four-acceleration]]). Then:

**(i)** the reading of the ideal clock between parameter values $s_1 < s_2$
equals $\tau(s_2)-\tau(s_1)$;

**(ii)** $\eta(U,U) = -c^{2}$ everywhere, so $U$ is future timelike with velocity units, and the dimensionless
vector $U/c$ is future unit timelike;

**(iii)** if $x$ is $C^{2}$ at $s$, then $\eta(U(s),A(s)) = 0$ and $A(s)$ is
zero or spacelike, with the unit of acceleration;

**(iv)** if the clock is free (subject to no interaction), then its
four-velocity is constant along the worldline and $A = 0$ identically;

**(v)** for an ideal observer at the same event, described by a future unit
timelike vector $n = U_{o}/c$ with $\eta(n,n) = -1$, the clock's speed relative
to the observer is $|w| = c\sqrt{1-\gamma^{-2}}$ with
$\gamma = -\eta(n,U/c) \ge 1$, so it is strictly less than $c$, and
$\gamma = 1$ exactly when the clock's four-velocity equals the observer's.

**Scope and qualification.** This is a conditional statement about the adopted
model; it asserts no measurement outcome, contains no statistical inference, and
inherits the idealizations of the postulates (ideal point particles, ideal
clocks, flat spacetime, no gravitational or quantum effects).
items.strategy: Conditional deduction from the adopted premises; the mathematical content is thm-sr-proper-time-and-observer-decomposition. (i) is the clock hypothesis of post-sr-free-trajectories-and-clock-hypothesis together with the proper-time definition, restated for the page's worldline calculus. (ii) and (iii) are clauses (a) and (b) of thm-sr-proper-time-and-observer-decomposition, with U identified with the clock's four-velocity by the clock hypothesis; the identification supplies the physical meaning of U, the identities are mathematical. (iv) By the free-trajectory clause there are p and future timelike v with x(s) = p + (s - s_0)v; then x' = v is constant, tau' = c^{-1} sqrt(-eta(v,v)) is constant and positive, so U = x'/tau' is the constant vector c v/sqrt(-eta(v,v)), and A = U'/tau' = 0. (v) is clause (d) of the mathematical theorem, with the observer vector n allowed to be any future unit timelike vector; post-sr-inertial-covariance licenses the interpretation of observers and clocks as model objects and def-sr-si-units-and-coordinate-conventions fixes c and the units of the speed. The proof must not upgrade the conditional statement to a claim about nature and must carry the idealizations to the conclusion.

items.physical_scope: Ideal clocks and massive test particles in the flat classical special-relativity model: four-velocity of squared norm -c^2 (dimensionless U/c unit timelike), four-acceleration orthogonal to four-velocity, vanishing four-acceleration for free particles, and subluminal speed relative to every ideal observer. Conditional on the named postulates; excludes interactions and force laws, gravity, quantum effects, real apparatus corrections and all empirical claims.

items.title: Worked example: the clock at rest in an inertial chart
items.statement:
Worked computation. In an inertial chart of the model with $\eta_0 =
\operatorname{diag}(-1,1,1,1)$ let $c>0$ and $(a_1,a_2,a_3)\in\mathbb R^3$. For $t\in\mathbb R$ consider the coordinate worldline
$x(t) = (ct, a_1, a_2, a_3)$ of a clock at rest at the spatial position
$(a_1,a_2,a_3)$, parametrized by the coordinate time $t$. Then
$x'(t) = (c,0,0,0)$, so $-\eta(x',x') = c^{2}$ and the proper-time function is
$\tau(t)-\tau(t_0) = t-t_0$; the four-velocity is $U = x'/\tau' = (c,0,0,0)$,
with $\eta(U,U) = -c^{2}$, and the four-acceleration vanishes, $A = 0$.
Relative to the chart's observer $e_0$ the dimensionless four-velocity is
$u = U/c = (1,0,0,0) = e_0$, so $\gamma = -\eta(e_0,u) = 1$ and the relative
velocity is $w = c\,h(u)/\gamma = 0$: the clock is at rest in the chart.
items.strategy: Direct evaluation: the diagonal form applied to (c,0,0,0) gives -c^2, so the proper-time integrand is the constant c/c = 1 and tau is t - t_0; U = x'/tau' = (c,0,0,0) and U' = 0, so A = 0. The relative-velocity clauses are clauses (c) and (d) of thm-sr-proper-time-and-observer-decomposition evaluated at these vectors. Every step is a finite computation from the definitions.

items.title: Worked example: proper time and four-velocity of a straight worldline at beta = 3/5
items.statement:
Worked computation. In an inertial chart with $\eta_0 =
\operatorname{diag}(-1,1,1,1)$ let $c>0$ and, for $t\in\mathbb R$, consider the coordinate worldline
$x(t) = \bigl(ct, (3c/5)t, 0, 0\bigr)$, parametrized by coordinate time, which
describes a clock moving along the first spatial axis with speed $3c/5$. Then
$x'(t) = (c,3c/5,0,0)$ and $\eta(x',x') = -c^{2}+(9/25)c^{2} = -(16/25)c^{2}$,
so $\sqrt{-\eta(x',x')} = 4c/5$ and
$\tau(t)-\tau(t_0) = (4/5)(t-t_0)$: the moving clock runs slow by the factor
$4/5 = 1/\gamma$ with $\gamma = 5/4$. The four-velocity is
$U = x'/\tau' = (5/4)\bigl(c,3c/5,0,0\bigr) = (5c/4,3c/4,0,0)$, which satisfies
$\eta(U,U) = -25c^{2}/16+9c^{2}/16 = -c^{2}$, and the four-acceleration vanishes
because $U$ is constant: $A = 0$. The dimensionless four-velocity is
$u = U/c = (5/4,3/4,0,0)$; the split of clause (d) with $n = e_0$ gives
$\gamma = 5/4$ and relative velocity $w = (0,3c/5,0,0)\in e_0^{\perp}$, whose spatial coordinates are exactly the
coordinate velocity.
items.strategy: Direct finite computation: evaluate the diagonal form on x', obtain the constant integrand c^{-1}(4c/5) = 4/5, integrate over [t_0,t], divide to obtain U, and evaluate eta(U,U). The vanishing of A is the constancy of U. The split clauses are clause (d) of thm-sr-proper-time-and-observer-decomposition evaluated at u = (5/4,3/4,0,0) and n = e_0; all numbers are exact rationals.

items.title: Worked example: invariance of elapsed proper time under a cubic reparametrization
items.statement: Worked computation. In an inertial chart with eta_0 = diag(-1,1,1,1) let d := (5,3,0,0), a future timelike displacement with -eta(d,d) = 25 - 9 = 16 and sqrt(-eta(d,d)) = 4. (a) The worldline x(s) := s d on the parameter interval [1,8] has x'(s) = d, integrand sqrt(-eta(d,d)) = 4, and elapsed proper time tau(8) - tau(1) = (1/c) integral_1^8 4 ds = 28/c. (b) The reparametrization phi(u) := u^3 is a strictly increasing C^1 surjection of [1,2] onto [1,8]; its derivative 3u^2 is strictly positive throughout [1,2], so the reparametrized curve y(u) := x(u^3) = u^3 d has y'(u) = 3u^2 d, hence sqrt(-eta(y',y')) = 3u^2 sqrt(-eta(d,d)) = 12u^2, and elapsed proper time (1/c) integral_1^2 12u^2 du = (4/c)(8 - 1) = 28/c. The two elapsed times agree, as lem-sr-proper-time-reparametrization-invariance requires, and the proper-time function of x is tau(s) = 4s/c up to an additive constant, with inverse rho(tau) = c(tau - tau_0)/4, where tau_0 is the chosen additive constant. (c) Boundary check: instead take the same straight curve x(s)=s d on [-1,1] and phi(u)=u^3 on [-1,1]. This is a strictly increasing C^1 surjection, but y'(0)=0, so y is not a worldline of def-sr-regular-causal-curve-and-worldline. The broad length-integral identity nevertheless holds: integral_{-1}^{1} 12u^2 du=8=integral_{-1}^{1} 4 ds. No proper-time function of y is invoked outside its defining worldline domain.
items.strategy: Two independent exact computations of the same elapsed time: in (a) the integrand is the constant 4; in (b) the chain rule gives y' = 3u^2 d and the integrand 12u^2, whose integral over [1,2] is 28. The equality is the concrete instance of the invariance lemma, and the inverse function is read off the linear proper-time function. All arithmetic is rational. On [1,2], 3u^2>=3>0 verifies the strengthened worldline consequence. For the boundary interval [-1,1], differentiate u^3 d to obtain the zero tangent at zero, and integrate 12u^2 to get 8; this checks precisely the distinction between the broad substitution identity and the regular-worldline consequence.

items.title: Worked example: four-velocity and four-acceleration of uniform circular motion
items.statement:
Worked computation. In an inertial chart with $\eta_0 =
\operatorname{diag}(-1,1,1,1)$ let $c>0$, $R > 0$ and let $\omega$ be real with
$R|\omega| < c$. Here $\sin,\cos:\mathbb R\to\mathbb R$ are the everywhere-convergent real power-series functions of
[[def-sine-and-cosine-by-power-series]]; their derivatives are $\cos$ and $-\sin$
([[thm-sine-and-cosine-derivatives]]), and $\sin^2+\cos^2=1$
([[cor-trigonometric-parity-and-pythagorean-identity]]). For $t\in\mathbb R$, consider the coordinate worldline
$x(t) = \bigl(ct, R\cos(\omega t), R\sin(\omega t), 0\bigr)$, parametrized by
coordinate time: uniform circular motion in the first two spatial coordinates.
Then $w(t) = \bigl(-R\omega\sin(\omega t), R\omega\cos(\omega t), 0\bigr)$ has
$|w| = R|\omega|$, so $-\eta(x',x') = c^{2}-R^{2}\omega^{2}$ and the
proper-time factor is
$\tau' = c^{-1}\sqrt{c^{2}-R^{2}\omega^{2}} = 1/\gamma$ with
$\gamma := (1-R^{2}\omega^{2}/c^{2})^{-1/2}$; the four-velocity is
$U = \gamma\,(c,w)$. Since $|w|$ is constant, $\gamma$ is constant; the
coordinate acceleration is
$a(t) = \bigl(-R\omega^{2}\cos(\omega t), -R\omega^{2}\sin(\omega t), 0\bigr)$,
with $|a| = R\omega^{2}$ and $w \cdot a = 0$. By clause (e) of
[[thm-sr-proper-time-and-observer-decomposition]] the four-acceleration is
$A = (0,\gamma^{2}a)$, so $A^{0} = 0$, $\eta(U,A) = 0$ and
$\eta(A,A) = \gamma^{4}R^{2}\omega^{4} \ge 0$. Its magnitude is
$\gamma^{2}R\omega^{2}$; for $R > 0$ it is spacelike exactly when
$\omega \ne 0$, while $\omega = 0$ is the static limit with $\gamma = 1$,
$U = (c,0,0,0)$ and $A = 0$. Numerical specialization: if $R\omega = 3c/5$,
then $\gamma = 5/4$ and the magnitude of the four-acceleration is
$\gamma^{2}R\omega^{2} = (25/16)R\omega^{2} = (15c\omega)/16$.
items.strategy: Finite computation: differentiate the coordinate path, evaluate the diagonal quadratic form to get tau', read gamma, and apply clause (e) of the theorem with w.a = 0 to obtain A = gamma^2 a; the numerical values are exact rational multiples of c and omega. The acceleration is centripetal and orthogonal to the velocity, so the four-acceleration is orthogonal to the four-velocity by the theorem. Since R>0 and gamma>0, gamma^4 R^2 omega^4 is zero exactly when omega=0 and positive otherwise. At zero frequency the path is (ct,R,0,0) and both the coordinate and four-acceleration vanish. The specialization R omega=3c/5 has omega>0 and preserves the displayed exact value and acceleration units.

items.title: Worked example: splitting a four-velocity in an observer's rest frame
items.statement: Worked computation. In an inertial chart with eta_0 = diag(-1,1,1,1) let the observer be n = e_0 = (1,0,0,0) and let u = (5/4, 3/4, 0, 0), a future unit timelike vector: eta(u,u) = -25/16 + 9/16 = -1. Then gamma = -eta(n,u) = 5/4 >= 1, h(u) = u + eta(n,u) n = u - (5/4)(1,0,0,0) = (0, 3/4, 0, 0) lies in n^perp = span(e_1,e_2,e_3), and the relative velocity is w = c h(u)/gamma = (0, 3c/5, 0, 0). One checks u = gamma (n + w/c) = (5/4)(1, 3/5, 0, 0) and |w|^2 = 9c^2/25 = c^2 (1 - gamma^{-2}) = c^2 (1 - 16/25). Also h(h(u)) = h(u) and eta(n,h(u)) = 0. This four-velocity is the one of the clock with coordinate velocity (3c/5, 0, 0) in ex-sr-proper-time-of-a-straight-worldline.
items.strategy: Direct evaluation of clauses (c) and (d) of thm-sr-proper-time-and-observer-decomposition on the displayed vectors: the projection, its idempotence and its orthogonality to n, the split u = gamma(n + w/c) and the identity |w|^2 = c^2(1 - gamma^{-2}) are each finite computations with rational numbers.

items.title: Counterexample: a future null curve has no proper-time parametrization
items.statement:
**False claim:** every regular $C^{1}$ curve of the model admits a proper-time
parametrization, with strictly increasing proper-time function and normalized
timelike four-velocity.

The claim is refuted by a straight future null line. It is a regular future
curve whose tangent is null at every point, so the proper-time integrand
vanishes identically, its formal length integral is constant and cannot
serve as a parameter, and no unit timelike tangent can be attached to the
curve. The existence of this curve is exactly why
[[def-sr-proper-time]] carries the future timelike hypothesis and why null
rays need their own parametrization.
items.strategy: For k=(1,1,0,0), eta(k,k)=0 and x:R->A, x(s)=p+sk. Formal length L(s)=c^-1 integral_0^s 0=0 cannot parametrize it; def-sr-proper-time assigns no function to this null curve. Bilinearity keeps every scalar multiple null, excluding a normalized timelike tangent. Coordinates x_A(p)+(s,s,0,0) give geometric speed c, without a physical light premise.

items.title: Counterexample: the proper-time integrand of a spacelike curve is not real
items.statement:
**False claim:** the formula
$\tau(b) - \tau(a) = c^{-1}\int_a^b \sqrt{-\eta(x'(s),x'(s))}\,ds$ assigns an
elapsed clock time to every regular $C^{1}$ curve of the model.

The claim is refuted by a straight spacelike line: its tangent is spacelike at
every point, so $-\eta(x',x')$ is negative and the square root is not a real
number. A spacelike interval is not elapsed clock time; the geometric spacing
along the curve is its spacelike length, a different quantity.
items.strategy: Direct evaluation: the diagonal form on d gives +3, so the integrand -eta(d,d) is negative and has no real square root; hence the claim that the construction assigns a clock time to every regular curve is false. The final clause records which hypothesis of the definition excludes the case and that the spacelike length of the curve is a different quantity, not an elapsed time.

items.title: Counterexample: a past-directed parametrization of a timelike line is not a worldline
items.statement:
**False claim:** if a $C^{1}$ curve parametrizes a straight timelike line, then
it is a future timelike worldline of the model and the proper-time construction
gives the clock reading of its history.

The claim is refuted by orienting the parametrization backwards: the same
geometric line with the opposite parametrization has past timelike tangents, is
not a worldline of the model, and yet the proper-time integrand takes exactly
the same values as for the future-directed parametrization. This is why the
parametrization, and not merely the image of the curve, is part of the
definition of a worldline.
items.strategy: For d=(5,3,0,0) future timelike, eta(d,d)=-16. On [0,1] use x(s)=p-sd and z(s)=p-d+sd=x(1-s), with exactly the same image and opposite past/future tangents. Their formal quadratic density is 4, but only z is a model worldline; equality of densities supplies neither orientation nor clock behavior.
